current_scope: The integrated-engine summary documents a dev32 snapshot of lifecycle-owned query services, bounded density and voxel preview work, cache budgets, closed-grid water simulation and scene-only Spatial/FSR1 settings. It explicitly excludes block models, textures, vegetation, deposits and player edits from query meshes, and distinguishes the closed query water grid from the saved finite-water runtime. These distinctions are useful existing contracts. Its dev32 heading is a document epoch: the separately inspected pinned build properties identify dev77 source, while the work-state checkpoint identifies dev53; none of those labels alone proves a newly qualified runtime.
gaps: The summary already names ownership and bounded admission, but readers need the observable lifecycle consequences: which requests may finish after clear, which results may publish after close, what a dimension identity contains, and which party owns cancellation and executor shutdown. Those distinctions are scattered across later cache and terminal-query records.

Query occupancy, preview meshes, host rendering and actual-world simulation appear in one short list. Add a capability-status matrix so a future caller cannot infer that the query mesh is authoritative for edited terrain, collisions, water placement or lighting geometry. Preserve the explicit unavailable DLSS and frame-generation states.
proposed_additions: Document a host-adapter contract for world attachment, immutable query input identity, request coalescing, admission rejection, generation invalidation and terminal closure. Include a result envelope carrying world, profile and revision identity, plus the consumer's obligation to reject stale completion before publication.

Link the three configuration ownership examples to the central scope/path manifest: engine runtime cache settings, graphics upscaling preferences and authoritative world-generation profiles. Give each capability a source checkpoint, artifact checkpoint and last native evidence reference, with this summary's historical epoch retained.
acceptance_checks: Use blocked and inline caller executors to verify close cannot be held behind terrain computation, terminal caches stay sealed, same-key work reserves capacity once and distinct dimensions never alias. Verify caller-owned executors remain usable after engine closure.

Trace one real saved generator into the query facade and confirm matching range, options and revision. Separately inspect a player-edited chunk and prove documentation never presents the unedited query preview as current materialized geometry. Verify unavailable providers remain visibly unavailable.

current_scope: The root README is a combined development-status, installation and player-operation guide. It declares Minecraft 26.1.2, NeoForge 26.1.2.122 and Java 25; describes original V7 terrain, finite water, actual-chunk LOD, custom video settings, optional Vulkan packaging and frozen generation profiles; and records unfinished V8 and broader engine acceptance. Its dev32 development label is stale relative to pinned gradle.properties dev77. The dev53 work-state checkpoint and owner-confirmed playable snapshots belong to separate evidence chains. This review preserves those discrepancies instead of treating the README label as current source or silently upgrading its capability claims.
gaps: The README already warns about experimental scope and old grades. It needs a compact current-source versus tested-artifact versus delivered-artifact table, because source-only V8 changes cannot inherit the native evidence of earlier installers. Installation directions should also distinguish lean OpenGL packaging, a Vulkan-capable profile, actual selected backend and recovery fallback.

The documented flat worldgen configuration and newer domain-based engine/upscaling files need an ownership and migration link. The configuration design is explicit that migration is unfinished; therefore changing every displayed path without a verified migration would give users false operating instructions. The same care applies to bundled versus standalone Themes and the independent Maritime project.
proposed_additions: Add a short status panel generated from a declared documentation snapshot: source SHA/version, known qualified artifact hash, target toolchain, generation-profile compatibility and links to the discrepancy register. Keep old validation statements under their named epoch and label the 906 occupancy disagreements as historical stage evidence until superseding native proof exists.

Add an operational compatibility matrix for root-only launch tasks, nested modules, clean profile installation, saved-world generation identity and requested/effective graphics API. Explain actual-chunk LOD's explored-data boundary and separate visual interpolation from authoritative host-tick simulation.
acceptance_checks: Compare the README status panel with pinned build properties and the artifact manifest rather than a moving branch label. Verify every download/install instruction names the artifact it actually describes, and that the standalone Themes JAR is not installed alongside its bundled duplicate.

Exercise the documented root task and profile choices in a disposable instance, check actual backend selection, and reopen a saved V1–V7 profile without silently changing future chunk generation. Treat this documentation batch as evidence review, not a new execution receipt.

current_scope: Recovery of the interrupted alpha 14 water and weather work, including speed-band currents and a narrowly scoped native normalization hook. This is a historical record for its named source and candidate; its results are not current verification.
gaps: The recorded boundary is that the missing installer hash is a recovery reference and earlier daylight observations do not certify the reconstructed build. Later summaries need to preserve that boundary when reusing this evidence.
proposed_additions: Add a recovery ledger that distinguishes source reconstruction, rebuilt artifacts, nested-module audits and actual delivery. This is a proposed enduring contract, not a claim that the historical defect is still present.
acceptance_checks: Rebuild the identified source, check the four nested modules and repeat current-force controls without adding duplicate boat acceleration. Record the new source, fixture and artifact identities before upgrading the evidence status.

current_scope: The loss of uncommitted alpha 16 work while published alpha 15 remained intact, with reconstruction anchored to a5af7b2684063c95c8a82bc2a306aefe824b26d4. This is a historical record for its named source and candidate; its results are not current verification.
gaps: The recorded boundary is that observations from the removed build do not automatically apply to reconstruction, and reference mods are not implemented features. Later summaries need to preserve that boundary when reusing this evidence.
proposed_additions: Add an immutable incident-to-reconstruction chain linking the recovered commit, new build, repeated checks and delivered bytes. This is a proposed enduring contract, not a claim that the historical defect is still present.
acceptance_checks: Reproduce each acceptance claim against the rebuilt installer and verify that the feature checklist never substitutes references for implementation evidence. Record the new source, fixture and artifact identities before upgrading the evidence status.

current_scope: The alpha 25 merged installer bringing eight branch heads into ancestry, bundling GUI Themes alpha 8 and retaining Maritime as a separate incompatible 1.21.1 project. This is a historical record for its named source and candidate; its results are not current verification.
gaps: The recorded boundary is that Linux Mesa native Journal checks do not establish Windows owner-GPU performance or make the Maritime directory loadable in the root installer. Later summaries need to preserve that boundary when reusing this evidence.
proposed_additions: Add a consolidation matrix separating ancestry inclusion, conflict decisions, nested-module presence and independently tested runtime environments. This is a proposed enduring contract, not a claim that the historical defect is still present.
acceptance_checks: Audit the assembled profile for duplicate Themes modules, repeat Journal navigation and GUI scaling, and verify Maritime remains outside the 26.1.2 runtime classpath. Record the new source, fixture and artifact identities before upgrading the evidence status.

current_scope: This is an unusually detailed design contract for domain-organized configuration, flexible ore deposits and a possible external editor, anchored to an alpha21 source snapshot. It already covers CLIENT/COMMON/STARTUP/SERVER scope, legacy backups and conflicts, canonical ownership, typed occurrence and composition controls, deterministic compiled planning, datapack/config/script routes, immutable world identity, offline registry uncertainty, staged editing and atomic saves. It expressly says the migration, ore API and editor are not shipped. Expansion should formalize and make these existing requirements executable, rather than presenting already documented controls as missing features.
gaps: The migration checklist needs a per-file state machine: discovery, parsed validation, destination conflict, backup verification, installation, activation and resumable interruption. Unknown future keys require a policy distinguishing lossless editor preservation from runtime rejection. Existing populated canonical files must remain authoritative, with a visible conflict report rather than hidden merge heuristics.

Equivalent authoring routes need a canonical compiled-definition identity. A schema-valid file can still reference an unavailable tag, unbounded candidate radius, unsupported shape or nondeterministic script result. Preview confidence also needs the exact registry manifest, generator revision, seed and unit interpretation, rather than one undifferentiated green validation result.
proposed_additions: Define a shared metadata registry for key path, type, units, default, scope, owner, constraints, dependency conditions and apply mode. Generate documentation and editor controls from it, while keeping semantic compilation in portable engine code and filesystem/reload effects in host adapters. Preserve exact numeric entry alongside sliders.

Specify a content-addressed compiled pack manifest and an explicit world-profile freeze operation. Add a compare-and-swap file save using the hash read at editor-open time, a verified backup, temporary sibling output and recoverable journal. Give offline ID checks separate verified, unknown and rejected statuses.
acceptance_checks: Interrupt migration at every state, start with old and new files together, use read-only destinations and missing optional modules, then prove values are not lost and one live authority remains. Test dedicated-server scope and templates using actual host behavior.

Compile equivalent deposit definitions through each implemented route and compare canonical identity and sampled output. Bound large definitions and preview workers, verify chunk-order/restart determinism, preserve depleted or removed deposits, and refuse to label approximate or unknown-registry previews as native equivalence.
source_anchors: # Configuration, flexible ore deposits and visual authoring

current_scope: MODULES describes an alpha24 packaging and dependency snapshot: portable core, performance, graphics, LOD and optional Vulkan modules, root host adapters and a single assembled installer with nested payloads. It already states important import directions, one-time configuration registration, safe optional LOD access and platform-specific bundle choices. Historical ownership notes explain changes from earlier alphas. The document is valuable architecture evidence, but its alpha24 module/status statements must be reconciled with later source and GUI bundling rather than treated as a verified inventory of the pinned dev77 tree.
gaps: Compile-time import direction does not fully specify runtime ownership. The next contract should identify who creates and closes executors, native handles, caches, world listeners, config registrations and reload callbacks. Optional absence must be safe before class loading as well as after a capability query returns false.

Runtime JAR modules, proposed data-driven gameplay modules and optional external authoring tools are different dependency systems. The document should distinguish them explicitly. Disabling a gameplay feature must not remove registered block IDs from an existing save, while omitting a renderer backend must not force native-library initialization in common settings code.
proposed_additions: Add a module manifest with owner, public service interfaces, hard dependencies, optional capabilities, config scopes, lifecycle hooks, host requirements and package profiles. Link each entry to its actual build target and mark the manifest's source epoch. Keep the present platform-neutral core and host-adapter direction intact.

Define optional-service behavior through stable interfaces and explicit unavailable results, including shutdown and world-switch ordering. Add a packaging closure table for lean, platform Vulkan, universal, no-LOD and bundled-Themes variants, plus a separate standalone-authoring executable that consumes schemas without loading the game.
acceptance_checks: Extend existing import-boundary checks with classpath and initialization checks: start a dedicated server without client natives, start without LOD or Vulkan, and ensure settings access never initializes an omitted backend. Audit nested modules for duplicate classes and stable declared versions.

Open and close two worlds with requests in flight, reload resources, and verify each module releases only its owned work and resources. Confirm disabled data features retain save identity and fail with actionable dependency diagnostics rather than silently deleting or replacing content.

current_scope: The block-texture plan records the owner's 32×32 default for block and item tiles, with 64×64 reserved for justified detail and UI/background artwork treated separately. It distinguishes a 1,013-row concept catalog from actual asset requirements, promotes shared grayscale families and material-by-shape reuse, and explicitly protects approved ground-v4 and final-sand bytes. Its two candidate batches total 110 exports, with 88 rock rows mapped to 81 unique candidates. Native lighting, mip, orientation, reload and near/far acceptance remain pending; contact sheets and reduced-screen studies are documented as screening evidence.
gaps: The plan already separates catalog entries from files, but a machine-readable many-to-many crosswalk would prevent later counts from becoming false completion claims. Aliases, chemical minerals, rock families, processed forms, block faces and gameplay registrations should have different identity fields instead of relying on an asset filename to carry all meanings.

A 64-pixel exception needs a recorded reason and approval state. The owner's default does not authorize downsampling protected 64-pixel ground faces, masks or sand. New 32-pixel comparisons must remain candidates until reviewed. Likewise, source approval, export correctness and native rendering acceptance are three distinct milestones.
proposed_additions: Create an asset ledger containing stable asset ID, material family, face/shape role, source master identity, decoded-pixel hash, export recipe, resolution justification, tint channels, alpha meaning, mip policy and approval state. Add explicit candidate, approved source, export verified, native verified, superseded and rejected states with evidence links.

Define material-family rules for neutral luminance, recognizable grain scale and directional faces, plus a shape system that reuses approved material inputs without flattening all rocks into one generic texture. Preserve argillite's provisional mapping and dolomite/dolostone taxonomy distinctions until their content owners resolve them.
acceptance_checks: Validate crosswalk cardinalities without assuming one row equals one tile or one tile equals one registered block. Hash protected v4 and sand assets before and after any pipeline work, and require explicit new approval before changing their bytes or resolution.

Build native review scenes covering repeated walls and floors, orientation, tint range, mips, cutout silhouettes, varied illumination and both graphics backends. Record actual display footprint and resource-pack precedence, then attach owner art review separately from numerical seam screening.
source_anchors: # Deep Primal block texture ownership and production plan

current_scope: Batch01 documents 40 actual 32-pixel candidate PNGs: 34 opaque bases and six binary-alpha cutouts. It records the master bundle, source hashes, export recipe and tools, a pine-plank revision, manifests and preview evidence. It carefully distinguishes opaque glacier ice from a translucent material implementation and opaque lichen/moss bases from masks. The source masters remain outside Git, while exported tile bytes are authoritative. The batch is candidate art: numerical and repeated-image screening do not establish native cutout mip behavior, tint integration or a complete set of wood and plant faces.
gaps: The recipe is unusually explicit, but reproducibility requires separating exact file identity from decoded-pixel identity. Encoder metadata or library changes can alter PNG bytes without changing pixels; conversely, a successful export command can still select the wrong master or role. The manifest should record both identities and all input dependencies.

The six cutouts need per-role alpha and mip rules. A hard 50-percent export threshold is a source conversion choice, not proof that distant foliage remains legible. Opaque ice, end grain, needles and kelp also need separate runtime face/material decisions instead of inheriting assumptions from a shared contact sheet.
proposed_additions: Add per-asset role cards linking exact source panel, crop, grayscale/tint expectations, opaque or cutout classification and permitted reuse. Include source bundle availability and restoration instructions without asserting that a restoration was tested unless it actually was. Keep partial exports rejected when masters are missing.

Define a promotion package containing the candidate manifest, source/export hashes, contact sheets, native scene recipe and owner approval. Preserve the recorded source generation and pine-plank revision rather than regenerating art procedurally or repainting seams to force an automatic metric to pass.
acceptance_checks: Reproduce into an isolated destination with all masters present, compare expected decoded pixels and exact delivered bytes, and fail before writing a partial manifest when an input is absent. Record tool versions and any intentional encoder normalization separately.

Render cutouts at near and distant footprints under actual game mip generation, review leaf and needle silhouettes, verify host-rock tint for the vein mask and inspect correct wood-face orientation. Treat ice translucency as a separate material feature with its own acceptance.

current_scope: Batch02 adds 70 opaque grayscale 32-pixel candidates, bringing both batches to 110 exports. Its rock coverage distinguishes 88 catalog rows from 81 unique candidate bases, including 11 reused Batch01 assets; the separate generic-coal comparison reference is not an additional coverage asset. The document records master-bundle identity, isolated export requirements, Box resampling and contact-sheet screening. It preserves provisional argillite, dolostone naming and grouped evaporite decisions. Native game, tint, lighting, near/far, mip and resource-reload checks are still pending despite the substantial source and export documentation.
gaps: The coverage counts are easy to misuse unless the manifest represents reused assets, aliases and comparison-only references explicitly. A copied reference texture should retain the same stable source identity rather than appear to be a newly authored candidate. Multiple rock names sharing a base do not imply their gameplay or physical properties are identical.

The edge-to-interior contrast threshold is a screening heuristic. It cannot decide whether a tile's structure, grain direction or repetition reads naturally in a large wall, or whether distinct coal ranks remain recognizable after tint and lighting. Reduced preview images also do not reproduce native sampler and mip behavior.
proposed_additions: Extend assets.json with role, reuse source, comparison-only status, provisional taxonomy reason and review evidence. Generate the coverage table from this crosswalk while preserving authored explanations. Add explicit approval transitions so source verification and coverage mapping never automatically publish resources into the runtime pack.

Create a native rock-family review suite containing large tiled planes, columns, stair faces, contrasting light directions and neutral versus final tint. Include deliberate comparisons for the coal ranks, mixed ironstone/banded iron and weathered versus fine-grained families rather than inspecting all candidates only at enlarged contact-sheet scale.
acceptance_checks: Verify the 70 new plus 11 reused bases map to the documented 88 rows, with the generic-coal reference excluded from production coverage. Require all master inputs before export and compare both decoded pixels and candidate file hashes.

Record actual native captures at selected screen footprints and graphics settings, review repetition and identity under changing light, and check resource reload. Keep a failed visual review as a rejected candidate even if the automated edge metric passes.

current_scope: The rock coverage table maps 44 legacy and 44 additional rows to the candidate grayscale bases. It explicitly handles grouped entries, reused materials and provisional choices: dolomite rock maps to dolostone rather than a mineral tile; lignite, bituminous and anthracite are distinct, with subbituminous added separately; some ironstone, eclogite and granulite entries reuse established bases; argillite provisionally reuses mudstone; and the evaporite umbrella resolves to halite/gypsum rather than inventing a third file. This is an asset crosswalk, not a declaration that all 88 rocks are registered, balanced, generated or visually accepted in the game.
gaps: The table is rich in human explanations but needs stable IDs and relationship types to prevent accidental collapse of taxonomy, gameplay definition and texture identity. A broad catalog row can intentionally resolve to multiple variants, while multiple rows can reuse one visual base. Those are different relationships with different runtime consequences.

Provisional mappings require a decision owner and promotion condition. Without that state, a temporary reuse can become permanent through copy-and-paste, or a future texture replacement can unexpectedly alter every dependent family. Native acceptance and source approval should be attached to asset versions rather than inferred from table coverage.
proposed_additions: Represent catalog row, material definition, visual family, texture asset and face/shape binding as separate stable identities. Give each crosswalk edge a role such as exact base, shared family, provisional substitute, grouped expansion or comparison only. Generate counts from unique identities and document why they differ.

Add an explicit variant-selection contract for grouped rows: deterministic seed or authored rule, valid host or process context, and no silent alteration of saved generation. Keep physical properties and ore/mineral taxonomy in their domain schemas so a shared texture never assigns composition or behavior by filename.
acceptance_checks: Resolve every row to existing candidate files and detect dangling references, duplicated IDs and accidental promotion of the generic-coal comparison. Verify the expected 88-row/81-base relationship while allowing legitimate many-to-many mappings.

Review argillite and umbrella evaporite decisions explicitly, inspect distinct coal ranks and grouped families under final tint, and check that replacing one visual asset updates only declared dependents. Require separate runtime registration and generation evidence before calling the catalog implemented.

current_scope: The ground-v2 README combines original approved source/crop details with later dev3 and dev4 integration records. It describes six grayscale 64-pixel faces, four complementary masks, opt-in sample ground blocks, provisional tints and the later generated dual-tint atlas/shader representation. Its alpha-like channel is blend data rather than transparency, and its recorded checks distinguish inventory/reload pixels from complete world-scene acceptance. The accumulated chronology contains references to v3 that are superseded by the later approved v4 source restoration. This document should remain historical evidence while a current asset manifest points to v4 and unchanged final sand.
gaps: The source and integration timelines need explicit status at each section. Statements that masks are not consumed describe an earlier stage; later shader integration describes another. Neither should be silently erased, but readers need a current pointer to prevent the rejected v3 art or old crops from being promoted accidentally.

The dual-tint representation already documents complementary masks, premultiplied soil contribution and linear mip treatment. Expansion should turn those details into a channel contract covering color-space conversion, rounding, alpha-as-data, shader marker ownership and behavior in third-party or fallback render paths. Numerical export checks do not establish all biome/light combinations.
proposed_additions: Add an art/source/integration chronology with immutable hashes and separate approval states. Link each dev3/dev4 result to its exact inputs, source and native fixture rather than letting a newer asset directory inherit every prior pass. Make the active manifest select the approved v4 faces and masks explicitly.

Specify the dual-tint equation and channel packing in one material-interface reference used by exporter, mip generator and every applicable shader path. State that grass/soil weights are not coverage alpha and that masks must not be passed through generic cutout processing or color-texture conversion.
acceptance_checks: Compare generated material inputs with their approved source pixels, verify mask complements and supported rounding, and run constant-color controls that detect double tinting, color-space errors and opacity misuse. Check model, item, entity and terrain paths individually.

Capture actual placed ground under several biome tints, AO/light conditions, distances and GL/Vulkan resource reloads. Preserve the historical inventory-only limits and do not infer world generation, spreading grass or farmland mechanics from the three opt-in sample block registrations.

current_scope: The ground-v3 document records a superseded attempt to remove a dark top cap by regenerating and processing side textures, including grayscale conversion, blur subtraction/recentering, shallow complementary masks and retained sand. It explicitly separates CPU/source proof from runtime material and native validation. Subsequent owner direction rejected the pale, sandy/noisy appearance and restored approved-source v4 artwork. Therefore v3 is useful negative design evidence and a reproducible experiment, not the current approved ground asset or a starting point for automatic 32-pixel conversion.
gaps: The source-specific rejection should be visible before the recipe so a reader cannot mistake a technically reproducible export for an approved visual target. Border continuity and matching soil rows were measured, but those metrics did not capture the loss of intended grain and root structure. That difference belongs in the acceptance rationale.

The document's original statements about masks not yet used and no fresh native validation belong to that experiment's time. Later shader work should not be back-projected into the v3 evidence. Keeping a clear link to v4 avoids treating a newer renderer as retrospective approval of rejected artwork.
proposed_additions: Add a superseded/rejected asset-state record naming the owner-observed visual problem, exact source/export identity and approved successor. Preserve the recipe and source evidence for traceability while excluding these bytes from current runtime manifests and from any generic latest-directory selection rule.

Use this attempt as a negative art-review fixture: automated seams, complementary masks and grayscale consistency may all pass while the result fails the intended material character. Require structural grain, side-root transition and broad-field repetition review alongside export validation, with separate decisions for source quality and renderer correctness.
acceptance_checks: Verify current manifests resolve to v4 and final sand rather than v3, and that a rebuild cannot accidentally choose assets by directory date or lexical order. Confirm protected current assets remain byte-identical when this historical experiment is archived or documented.

Reproduce v3 only in an isolated comparison destination when needed, label its images rejected, and compare owner-visible structure at native scale. Do not promote it merely because repeat-edge or mask arithmetic tests pass, and do not claim a new native test unless run.

current_scope: Ground-v4 restores the approved source after the rejected v3 appearance. It uses defined source crops for tops and sides, preserves characteristic grain and roots, joins to approved soil, removes the v3 blur/recenter/regenerated-source treatment and retains grayscale RGB8 plus complementary mask data. The manifest selects v4 with unchanged final sand. Recorded interior-pixel, hash and Java ImageIO checks support source/export identity; the document expressly does not claim a fresh complete build, native visual review, performance result or newly qualified installer. These 64-pixel assets are protected exceptions to the newer 32-pixel default.
gaps: The document clearly explains the restoration, but the current asset registry should capture approval as immutable versioned provenance rather than a directory name. Any proposed 32-pixel counterpart needs its own comparison and owner decision; it cannot replace approved 64-pixel bytes through a generalized resampling rule.

Matching interior crops and valid RGB loading do not establish all side joins under actual tint, mips and lighting. The unchanged dual-tint shader contract needs a direct reference so source masks, generated packed channels and runtime shader behavior cannot evolve independently while each local check still passes.
proposed_additions: Make v4 the explicit approved-source entry in the asset ledger, with hashes for every face and mask, retained source crop coordinates, export dimensions and a reason for the 64-pixel exception. Record v3 as rejected and v2 as historical integration evidence rather than deleting their useful provenance.

Add a promotion receipt that separately names source approval, decoded-pixel verification, generated-resource identity and native scene acceptance. Link soil/cover masks to the single dual-tint interface and state the intended side orientation, below-ground mask behavior and unchanged sand dependency.
acceptance_checks: Re-run pixel and complementary-mask controls using the exact approved crop inputs, compare delivered PNG and decoded-pixel hashes and detect any unintended inclusion of v3 overlays. Preserve current bytes while experimenting with alternate resolutions in a separate candidate path.

Place repeated ground blocks in native scenes with different tints, exposed sides, seams, mips and both graphics APIs. Verify reload and generated-atlas identity against the same manifest. Treat visually approved source as necessary but separate from native shader and package acceptance.
source_anchors: # Restore approved ground art at the intended feature scale

current_scope: The final-sand README defines a protected 64-pixel grayscale, low-contrast, nondirectional fine-grain source intended for all faces with tint and no mask. It records its generated master, wrapped resampling and repeated-image proof. It does not claim native rendering, stochastic variants or a cross-blend implementation. Although short, this document establishes a concrete approved material direction that the broader texture pipeline must preserve. The 32-pixel default in the later texture plan calls for comparisons where useful, not automatic replacement or downsampling of this approved sand.
gaps: The one-tile, all-face choice needs a stable material and source identity in the shared asset ledger so later family-generation tools do not replace it with directional noise or a procedural default. Resolution exception, approval status, tint role and absence of coverage masks should be explicit fields rather than inferred from prose.

Wrapped resampling and repeat-proof bytes establish a particular export process, but they do not establish visual isotropy under lighting, mip stability, native color handling or the appropriate contrast over a broad landscape. Those acceptance categories should remain distinct from the recorded source/export checks.
proposed_additions: Add a sand role card with canonical source master, crop/resampling recipe, exact PNG and decoded-pixel hashes, 64-pixel exception rationale, neutral luminance expectations and all-face binding. Keep any 32-pixel study as a new unapproved candidate linked to this source, with explicit promotion criteria.

Define how the runtime applies sand tint in linear shading and which material parameters belong to the shader rather than being painted into albedo. Preserve the intended low-contrast fine grain; additional wetness, beach variation or stochastic sampling should be separate proposed features with their own saved/material compatibility and visual review.
acceptance_checks: Verify the same approved tile is bound to every intended sand face and no alpha-mask or organic-ground blend rule is accidentally applied. Re-export in isolation and compare the recorded repeat and pixel identities without modifying the approved runtime resource.

Review large native sand planes and slopes at near and distant footprints, with multiple sun angles, tints and mip levels on GL and Vulkan. Record whether grain becomes directional or noisy. Require owner approval before replacing the source, resolution or broad material character.

current_scope: The colormap README documents first-pass palettes for three opaque 256×256 RGB lookups and 40 existing water biome colors, with isolated export and exact resource checks. It explains the intentional Minecraft namespace required by existing loaders and the possible effect on other compatible worlds. It also distinguishes visual tint from GradientPalette's ordered material-ID fields and labels those V8 preview paths unregistered. The 40 mapped runtime profiles are not the full 118 proposed profiles. Some side-tint status text belongs to an earlier integration epoch and needs a pointer to later dual-tint evidence.
gaps: The namespace choice makes resource priority and cross-world reach an operational requirement. A valid pack can affect more than Deep Primal terrain, so acceptance should identify the exact loader, biome lookup and active pack stack. Headless resource equality does not prove runtime lookup coordinates, reload behavior or final lighting appearance.

Color lookup values and material-gradient IDs need separate schemas and revision identities. The former changes visual output, while the latter can change generated block identity and save compatibility. A shared word such as palette should not obscure those different ownership and migration rules.
proposed_additions: Add a palette manifest naming lookup dimensions, color encoding, coordinate convention, expected loader, namespace, source definition and approval state. Track the 40 existing biome mappings explicitly and leave proposed profiles unverified until registered and reviewed. Link current dual-tint integration rather than rewriting historical observations as fresh results.

Give visual tint and material-ID gradients separate authoring panels and compiler outputs. Material gradients require stable IDs, deterministic spatial variation and saved generator identity; visual palettes require runtime resource precedence and color-space checks. An offline editor should show which kind of output the user is changing before Apply.
acceptance_checks: Load the pack through the actual target game, sample known climate coordinates and biome water entries, switch pack priority and reload. Verify the documented namespace behavior in both Deep Primal and another compatible world rather than assuming isolation.

Compare exact exported resources with the manifest, inspect tint under real light and mips, and verify changing a visual palette never changes material IDs. Keep V8 material preview results separate from frozen V1–V7 generation and from owner approval of final color direction.

current_scope: The decision ledger records owner-confirmed direction that supersedes older draft ideas while expressly remaining separate from implementation proof. It covers expanded-height performance boundaries, biome-first planning, configuration organization, noncircular early progression, finite water and regional recharge, physical cargo, local storage, calendar behavior, exploration permissions, complete replacement of vanilla XP, finite ore depletion, inventory recovery and optional power integration. It includes nonnegotiable rules such as no vanilla-XP compatibility pool, alongside tunable future mechanics. Its final alpha6 renderer discussion belongs to an older epoch and must not override later Vulkan-capable source and validation records.
gaps: The decisions are rich but need stable IDs, precedence, effective date and explicit implementation/evidence links. Otherwise a later roadmap checkbox or old paragraph can appear to reopen a settled owner choice. Binding invariants, permitted tuning, unresolved design questions and delivery milestones should be distinguished without weakening the actual decisions.

Several domains share transactional ownership problems: finite water, ore depletion, cargo recovery, nested inventory and animal processing must not duplicate or lose resources across retries. The ledger states intended behavior but needs a common vocabulary for authoritative commands, idempotency, persistent identity and unresolved compensation rather than independent informal exceptions.

The calendar's pause/no-offline-catch-up policy should not be extrapolated to every clock. Simulation ticks, environmental intervals, presentation interpolation and any deliberately real-time cooldown need named semantics. Exploration permissions likewise belong on the server's disclosed data, not merely in a client overlay's visibility toggle.
proposed_additions: Create a decision register with immutable decision ID, owner wording reference, scope, superseded decision, config allowance, implementation owner and acceptance evidence. Link it from design-reference and roadmap sections. Mark dated renderer/platform passages as historical context and use the discrepancy ledger for reconciliation.

Add shared command contracts for persistent resources: expected revision, authoritative owner, validation-before-mutation, committed result identity, retry behavior and recovery state. Define map discovery and capability disclosure separately from rendering. Keep cargo physical mass and local-only storage rules visible in every relevant integration contract.

Add a clock-domain table and a scope checklist for each release milestone. Proposed refinements may improve verification or resolve ambiguity, but should not silently add large gameplay systems to the approved first release or turn fixed XP and world-identity rules into optional compatibility settings.
acceptance_checks: Trace every binding decision to its affected schema or subsystem and verify newer prose does not contradict it. Test nested inventory/cargo retries, ore depletion and processing for duplicate outcomes, and ensure optional integrations preserve native units and authority rather than becoming required dependencies.

Pause and reopen a server under the chosen clock policy, check private versus shared exploration at the network boundary, and verify disabling custom HUD presentation never restores vanilla XP inside Deep Primal. Record unimplemented decisions as requirements, not passed behavior.
source_anchors: # Deep Primal — Design Decisions and Proposals

current_scope: The v0.6 design reference is a broad draft defining the long-term modular survival sandbox, platform-neutral core direction, property registries, shared services, gameplay modules, authoring routes, materials, field guide, inventory and worldgen. It already distinguishes stable registrations from enabled features, proposes manifests and frozen world settings, and includes later actual-chunk LOD direction. However its early tables, roadmap and open questions retain older heightmap-LOD and undecided-platform language. Some future external-platform assertions are exploratory references, not verified port commitments. The document must be expanded as a versioned design reference, not relabeled as a description of the pinned implementation.
gaps: Status varies by section: owner decisions, implemented module boundaries, experimental V8 components, future gameplay and unresolved external-platform possibilities are mixed. A section-level status overlay would let readers identify binding direction and evidence without deleting useful earlier reasoning. The confirmed target and later LOD decision should explicitly supersede stale open questions.

The proposed data-driven gameplay manifest needs separation from actual build modules. Registry identity, optional feature activation, dependency validation, per-world locks and inert disabled content must be specified independently. Likewise, a portable Java core does not by itself replace Minecraft storage, networking, lighting, input, audio, resource loading or lifecycle.

The material-by-shape and grayscale-family concepts need alignment with the approved 32/64 asset plan. Older procedural-texture language must not authorize regenerating approved ground and sand art. The field guide and inspection APIs also need server-side disclosure semantics, and inventory count/stack ideas must remain proposals until verified against the actual host.
proposed_additions: Add a design-status legend and a decision-linked section index: binding, proposed, source implemented, native qualified, superseded or unresolved. Reference current configuration/ore contracts instead of maintaining divergent control lists. Generate shared terminology for units, material properties, clocks and profile identity from a single schema owner.

Define three boundaries: authored source data and optional DCC tools; portable compilation and deterministic simulation; host adapters and client presentation. Give each proposed gameplay module a manifest with stable IDs, dependencies, authority, save behavior and enable/disable policy. Keep platform migration as a sequence of adapter replacements with evidence gates.

Add field-guide content IDs, locale and search metadata with explicit discovery permissions, and a material/shape crosswalk that limits authored asset duplication. Preserve source artwork approvals and distinguish visual variants from new physical material definitions.
acceptance_checks: Reconcile the selected platform, actual-chunk LOD and fixed XP policy with every summary table and open question, recording supersession rather than silently inventing new decisions. Verify all purported implementation statements link to a named source and appropriate evidence.

Disable a proposed feature in a saved-world fixture without removing registry identities, compile equivalent definitions through supported authoring routes, and ensure unauthorized exploration or inspection data is never sent to a client. Treat standalone runtime and external-editor execution as separate future qualification work.
